text:
Maya: putting up a quick Figma link for the model explorer iteration — mainly filters, the side-by-side compare table, performance badges, and the version-pinning flow. mind 2-min UX eyes? https://www.figma.com/file/xxxx/model-explorer
Diego: looked. overall 👍. two big calls: keep filters persistent across pages, and simplify badge language (short + tooltip).
Ravi: persistent filters make sense for power users. curious how it behaves for quick searches though — should we add a clear-all on search?
Maya: yes to clear-all. thinking: persistent state per org + per user toggle. quick searches should not auto-override unless user hits "apply".
Claire: re: compare table — the current dense grid is hard to scan. suggestion: add subtle row striping or stronger horizontal dividers and increase vertical padding by 4px. that will help readability without killing density.
Diego: prefer subtle striping (low contrast) over heavy dividers. but A11y concern: stripes must still meet contrast for edge cases.
A11yBot: quick flag — current badge color #f9e6c2 on white fails 4.5:1. Recommend darker fill or bold text + border. Also keyboard focus on table rows is missing (no visible outline).
Zach: noted. can do focus outline with `outline: 3px solid var(--focus)` for the row and add `tabindex="0"` on the row element. will also add `aria-selected` when rows are chosen for compare.
Maya: sample aria + CSS for review:
```css
.row:focus { outline: 3px solid var(--blue-500); background: rgba(14,114,199,0.04); }
.compare-badge { background: #0b5cff; color: #fff; padding: 2px 6px; border-radius: 6px; font-size: 12px; }
```
Diego: small copy nit for badges — instead of 'fast' / 'cheap' use 'p99 latency' and 'cost per 1k tokens' in tooltip; badge text stays one word: 'low-latency', 'low-cost' (kebab for compactness).
Ravi: +1. Also callout: when pinning a model version we need clearer affordance that pinning impacts routing (will send production requests). Maybe modal with two toggles: 'pin for this project' vs 'pin org-wide'.
Maya: current mock pins from the model-card header. suggestion: move "Pin" into a kebab menu and replace header action with a small pin icon that shows state. Clicking the icon opens a compact confirm sheet.
Claire: dev constraints: we need an API change for org-wide pin. if we add two-level pinning, let's keep client UX tiny — icon opens sheet with two radio options and an inline link to docs.
Diego: accessibility + microcopy for pin modal: header "Pin model version", helper text: "Routing for new requests will default to this version. Rollouts unaffected unless you enable automatic routing." Add a prominent danger color if it's org-wide.
A11yBot: additional: ensure pin control can be operated via keyboard and that the modal sets `aria-modal="true"` and focus trap. Provide screen reader text for the current pin state, e.g., `aria-live` announcement: 'Model v1.3 pinned for project'.
Zach: I'll prototype keyboard nav and the focus trap today. also will change badge color to meet contrast.
Maya: one more tiny UX ask — filters should show selected count (e.g., 'Quantized (3)') and allow keyboard to open/close chips.
Diego: agree. and add a clear visual for 'filters active' in the topbar, not just the chips. maybe a dot or numeric pill.
Ravi: plan: Diego + Zach iterate on color and spacing, Claire will check backend impact for org pins, Maya will update Figma and add microcopy, I'll schedule a 20-min review tomorrow.
Maya: perfect — thanks all. tagging follow-ups: @Zach for a PR, @Claire for API scope, @Diego for final copy. :thumbsup:
